title: A mode write to an unavailable select is recorded as made
claim: With the mode select, hot-water and space entities unavailable at a partial step's switch-on, the arbiter records the mode write in held.written (and reports it to duty_switch) although Home Assistant's entity service call skips an unavailable entity, on 5 of 5 rigs.
mechanism: pump_arbiter._write gates on 'state is None', never on state 'unavailable'; _lead_mode writes the step's mode ahead of the switch-on, services.async_call returns without error because Home Assistant leaves an unavailable entity out of the call, and held.written, _report_write (duty_switch.note_mode_write) and _persist record a write that never landed. The stub FakeServices records every call, so the suite cannot see it. The pump then starts in its previous mode; the next pass after the entity returns rewrites it (hold), so the cost is one tick and a phantom mode switch in the learner.

evidence.unit: rigs whose unavailable row records a skipped write as made
evidence.machine: box B11, Linux 6.18.44 x86_64, venv-ci CPython 3.14
evidence.contention_note: count; contention-immune (two other seats on the box)

perturbation.change: --perturb write_skips_unavailable: _write returns before the call when the slot's entity reads 'unavailable'

metric_definition: Rigs where a slot whose service call the Home Assistant emulation skipped (entity state 'unavailable') is in pump_arbiter.state_for(coord).written after the pass.
phenomenon_property: A write is recorded as made only when Home Assistant delivered it to an available entity.

null_control.note: the emulation without Home Assistant's skip (the stub's behaviour): no write is skipped and the count reads 0, so the count keys on the skip

proposed_fix_scope: pump_arbiter._write: treat an entity reading unavailable/unknown as no write (as state None); tests/hastub's FakeServices to skip unavailable entities as Home Assistant does (ha_contract row).
